nodes.title: Self-Awareness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify their own emotions, strengths, and areas for growth and explain how feelings affect their choices.

nodes.title: Personal Responsibility
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what it means to be responsible and give examples of owning their actions, chores, and mistakes.

nodes.title: Time Management
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan a simple schedule, prioritize tasks, and explain how to use a calendar or to-do list to meet a deadline.

nodes.title: Goal Setting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can set a specific, measurable goal and list the steps and timeline needed to reach it.

nodes.title: Decision Making
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can weigh options against pros, cons, and consequences and explain the reasoning behind a choice.

nodes.title: Problem Solving
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can define a problem, generate several solutions, test one, and evaluate whether it worked.

nodes.title: Basic Money Concepts
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify coins and bills, state their values, and make change for a small purchase.

nodes.title: Budgeting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can build a simple budget that balances income against expenses and explain why tracking spending matters.

nodes.title: Banking & Transactions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the purpose of a bank and describe how deposits, withdrawals, and transfers work.

nodes.title: Work Habits
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can demonstrate reliable work habits such as being on time, following directions, and finishing tasks.

nodes.title: Collaboration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can work with others toward a shared goal, contribute a fair share, and describe each member's role.

nodes.title: Conflict Resolution
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use calm, respectful strategies to resolve a disagreement and reach a compromise.

nodes.title: Professional Communication
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a clear professional email and speak appropriately in a formal or workplace setting.

nodes.title: Career Exploration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can research several careers, describe what each involves, and connect them to their own interests and strengths.

nodes.title: Job Readiness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can complete a job application and describe the steps of finding, applying for, and starting a job.

nodes.title: Independent Living Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe the everyday self-care and household tasks needed to live independently and explain why each matters.

nodes.title: Health & Wellness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how nutrition, exercise, sleep, and hygiene work together to keep the body and mind healthy.

nodes.title: Long-Term Planning
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can build a multi-year plan toward a major life goal and identify the milestones and resources required.

nodes.title: Financial Independence
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can outline a plan to support themselves financially, covering income, budgeting, saving, credit, and taxes.

nodes.title: Adult Responsibility
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe the core responsibilities of adult life and demonstrate the ability to manage them independently.

nodes.title: Entrepreneurship
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can develop a simple business idea, describe its customers and costs, and explain how it would make a profit.

nodes.title: Home Management
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan and carry out the routine tasks of running a household, including cleaning, upkeep, and supplies.

nodes.title: Digital Productivity
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use common digital tools (documents, email, calendars, search) to organize information and complete tasks.

nodes.title: Ethics & Integrity
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain what it means to act with honesty and integrity and evaluate a situation for the right thing to do.

nodes.title: Growth Mindset
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain that ability grows with effort and give an example of learning from a mistake instead of giving up.

nodes.title: Organization
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can keep their materials, files, and space in order and explain a system for finding what they need.

nodes.title: Resilience
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe strategies for coping with setbacks and explain how to bounce back and keep trying after a failure.

nodes.title: Self-Advocacy
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify their own needs and ask for help, accommodations, or resources in an appropriate way.

nodes.title: Active Listening
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can listen without interrupting, restate what a speaker said, and ask a relevant follow-up question.

nodes.title: Empathy
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can recognize how another person feels and describe a caring, respectful way to respond.

nodes.title: Assertiveness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can state their needs, opinions, and boundaries clearly and respectfully without being passive or aggressive.

nodes.title: Giving & Receiving Feedback
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can give specific, kind, useful feedback and accept feedback without becoming defensive.

nodes.title: Needs vs Wants
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish between needs and wants and sort everyday examples of each.

nodes.title: Saving vs Spending
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the difference between saving and spending and describe why setting money aside for a goal helps.

nodes.title: Comparison Shopping
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can compare price, quantity, and quality of similar products and identify the best value.

nodes.title: Paychecks & Deductions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can read a pay stub and explain the difference between gross and net pay and common deductions.

nodes.title: Credit & Debt
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how credit works, what debt is, and how a credit score is affected by borrowing and repayment.

nodes.title: Interest
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how interest is earned on savings and charged on loans and calculate a simple interest amount.

nodes.title: Taxes Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain why people pay taxes, name common types of taxes, and describe what filing a tax return involves.

nodes.title: Insurance Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how insurance spreads risk and describe common types such as health, auto, and renters insurance.

nodes.title: Investing Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how investing grows money over time and describe the trade-off between risk and return.

nodes.title: Avoiding Scams & Consumer Awareness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can recognize common scams and deceptive practices and describe how to protect their money and personal information.

nodes.title: Checking & Savings Accounts
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the difference between a checking and a savings account and describe how to open and use each.

nodes.title: Debit & Credit Cards
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain the difference between a debit and a credit card and describe the responsibilities of using each.

nodes.title: Online Banking & Digital Payments
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe how to bank online, send a digital payment, and keep account access secure.

nodes.title: Nutrition & Healthy Eating
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the major food groups and plan a balanced meal that supports good health.

nodes.title: Physical Fitness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain why regular exercise matters and describe activities that build strength, endurance, and flexibility.

nodes.title: Sleep & Hygiene
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe healthy sleep and personal hygiene routines and explain why each keeps the body well.

nodes.title: Mental Health & Stress Management
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can recognize signs of stress and describe healthy strategies for managing emotions and when to seek help.

nodes.title: Substance-Abuse Awareness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe the risks of alcohol, tobacco, and drug use and identify strategies for refusing and getting help.

nodes.title: First Aid & Safety Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can respond to a common minor injury and describe basic safety and emergency procedures, including when to call for help.

nodes.title: Cooking Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can follow a simple recipe safely, using basic kitchen tools and safe food-handling practices.

nodes.title: Meal Planning
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan a week of balanced meals and build a shopping list that fits a set budget.

nodes.title: Cleaning & Home Maintenance
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can carry out routine cleaning and describe basic home maintenance tasks and when to call for repairs.

nodes.title: Laundry
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can sort, wash, dry, and fold clothing correctly and read a garment care label.

nodes.title: Grocery Shopping
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can make a shopping list, find items in a store, and stay within a budget while comparing prices.

nodes.title: Transportation & Navigation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan a route using public transit or maps and describe safe, reliable ways to get where they need to go.

nodes.title: Renting & Housing Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how renting works, read the key terms of a lease, and describe the costs of housing.

nodes.title: Digital Citizenship & Online Safety
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe safe, respectful online behavior and explain how to protect privacy, passwords, and a positive digital footprint.

nodes.title: Resume Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a basic resume that lists their skills, experience, and education in a clear, organized format.

nodes.title: Interview Skills
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can prepare for a job interview, answer common questions clearly, and present themselves professionally.

nodes.title: Workplace Etiquette
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe professional behavior on the job, including punctuality, dress, communication, and respect for coworkers.

nodes.title: Networking
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how professional relationships lead to opportunities and describe how to build and maintain a network.

merges.note: LS8 Budgeting bundled the underlying saving-vs-spending idea. Retained as the base atomic (building/balancing a budget) and split out LS-321 Saving vs Spending as an elementary feeder below it. Original junk chain LS7->LS8 kept as a real within-strand prereq; the cross-strand upstream (LS6 Problem Solving -> LS7) that hard-locked all of financial literacy behind decision/problem-solving was dropped.

LS9 Banking & Transactions was a single coarse node covering several distinct assessable ideas. Retained as the base atomic (what a bank is / deposits-withdrawals-transfers) and decomposed into LS-330 Checking & Savings Accounts, LS-331 Debit & Credit Cards, and LS-332 Online Banking & Digital Payments. Original junk edge LS8->LS9 relaxed to soft (banking no longer strictly requires a completed budget); both now hard-depend only on LS7 Basic Money Concepts. Original hard lock LS9->LS10 (banking before work habits) dropped, and LS9->LS23 (banking before digital productivity) dropped.

LS19 Financial Independence was a coarse capstone bundling credit, taxes, insurance, and investing. Retained as the Mastery capstone (hard on LS8 Budgeting + LS9 Banking) and decomposed into LS-324 Credit & Debt, LS-326 Taxes Basics, LS-327 Insurance Basics, and LS-328 Investing Basics, now feeding it as soft_deps rather than being implied inside one node. Additional financial feeders added: LS-320 Needs vs Wants, LS-322 Comparison Shopping, LS-323 Paychecks & Deductions, LS-325 Interest, LS-329 Avoiding Scams & Consumer Awareness. Original junk chain LS17->LS18->LS19 (health hard-locking planning hard-locking finance) dropped; LS19 now built on the real money spine.

LS17 Health & Wellness was a single coarse node for all of health. Retained as the base atomic (how nutrition/exercise/sleep/hygiene fit together) and decomposed into LS-340 Nutrition & Healthy Eating, LS-341 Physical Fitness, LS-342 Sleep & Hygiene (early feeder), and LS-343 Mental Health & Stress Management. New health skills added alongside: LS-344 Substance-Abuse Awareness and LS-345 First Aid & Safety Basics. Original junk chain LS16->LS17->LS18 (independent living hard-locking health hard-locking planning) dropped; LS17 no longer requires independent living and is now a mid-elementary Application skill fed softly by its components.

LS16 Independent Living Basics bundled several distinct household skills. Retained as the base atomic (overview of self-care/household tasks) and decomposed into LS-350 Cooking Basics, LS-353 Laundry, and LS-354 Grocery Shopping. Further living skills added: LS-351 Meal Planning, LS-355 Transportation & Navigation, LS-356 Renting & Housing Basics (Cleaning & Home Maintenance split under LS22). Original junk edge LS15->LS16 (job readiness hard-locking independent living) dropped — LS16 no longer requires employment and is fed softly by LS2/LS3.

LS15 Job Readiness bundled the concrete job-seeking skills. Retained as the base atomic (finding/applying/starting a job) and decomposed into LS-370 Resume Basics, LS-371 Interview Skills, and LS-372 Workplace Etiquette. LS-373 Networking added new. Original junk edge LS13->LS14->LS15 spine relaxed: LS15 hard-depends only on LS14 Career Exploration, with LS10 Work Habits, LS13 Professional Communication, and LS23 Digital Productivity as soft_deps (the old LS23->LS15 leads_to became a soft dep).

LS22 Home Management bundled cleaning/upkeep. Retained as the base atomic and split out LS-352 Cleaning & Home Maintenance. LS22 keeps its real hard prereq on LS16; the original LS22->LS20 leads_to was converted to a soft dep on LS20 Adult Responsibility.

Structural fix: the original graph was a single linear hard-prereq spine LS1->LS2->...->LS20 (23 hard edges, 0 soft) that forced unrelated skills into one chain -- e.g. Banking (LS9) before Work Habits (LS10), Work Habits before Collaboration (LS11), Conflict Resolution (LS12) before Professional Communication (LS13), Job Readiness (LS15) before Independent Living (LS16), and Health (LS17) before Long-Term Planning (LS18) before Financial Independence (LS19). That spine was dismantled and re-grouped into seven real strands (Personal Development, Social & Communication Skills, Financial Literacy, Career & Work Readiness, Health & Wellness, Independent Living, Digital & Ethics). Cross-strand hard locks were converted to soft_deps and directions corrected (foundations before advanced; a concept before its application; basic money before budgeting before financial independence). Hard prereqs are now retained only within a strand's genuine build order. The four leads_to edges (LS21->LS20, LS22->LS20, LS23->LS15, LS24->LS20) were converted to soft_deps on their targets. Junk stage-name clusters (Foundations/Fluency/Application/Integration/Mastery) were replaced by the seven topical strands while stage/stage_id were preserved as the difficulty axis.

Coverage: 'teamwork' from the career/work benchmark is covered by existing LS11 Collaboration (not duplicated as a new node). LS11 was relocated out of the middle of the junk linear spine (it had been hard-locked behind Work Habits) to a Fluency (grade 3-6) social-skills foundation, fed softly by the new LS-310 Active Listening and LS-311 Empathy and feeding LS12 Conflict Resolution.
